located_point.method: Sentinel-2 composite renders at 3 km, 1.5 km and 700 m (RGB, NIR, brightness, edge). The archaeological area is the tree-covered, brown and bare textured ground of about 1 km by 1 km immediately south-west of the dense modern town of Harappa, matching Vats 1940 Plate I, where the mounds F, AB and E lie west and south-west of the town and south of the old bed of the Ravi. The point is the middle of that textured area; individual mounds could not be delimited with confidence at 10 m.

imagery_unmeasurable_reason: Features not resolvable at 10 m: no straight edge in the mound area could be tied to the granary, the workmen's quarters or any other wall on the plans; the area is broken by trees, paths and spoil.

sources.status: used for location only; no line measured

notes: Imagery: located but not measurable at 10 m. Plans: both plates are Mound F plans from Vats 1940 vol. II, each with an unspecified arrow, so their bearings are relative to their own arrows. Plate III (Great Granary): eleven faces of the Western Block's long east wall and of the long walls of five granary units in both blocks lie between -1.4 and -2.1 degrees from the plate's arrow; all are one system. Plate XI (Workmen's Quarters): eight faces of house walls and of the long wall between the two rows of houses lie between -0.7 and -3.1 degrees. The walls of both plates are drawn slightly off the page and grid axes, and both plates show the same small negative deviation relative to their arrows. Plate XI carries a 20 ft survey grid parallel to the page; we measured only wall faces and kept every corridor clear of the grid lines. Plate I (site plan, PDF page 14, plan library entry harappa-01) was used for identification only; it has an unspecified 'N' arrow and its legend states 'Magnetic Declination about 1 deg 55 min East in 1930. (Decreasing by about 3 min annually)', which suggests but does not state that the Plate I arrow is true north. We did not register Plate I to the imagery: the only shared features are modern roads and buildings whose 1930s and present positions we could not confirm.
